chapter_theme: The last song at Viralimalai (விராலிமலை, 2 of 2): drowned in the maya of women who deceive the body, the poet asks when Murugan will come running as guard before Yama's messengers bind his legs with their rope; the praise centres on Uma, one with Brahma, Vishnu and Siva, who gave Murugan.

583.reading: The poet says that, sinking in the maya of women whose breasts sway like Meru and who deceive the body, he has a fool's understanding, and asks on what day Murugan will come running as his guard to see his servant, so that Yama's messengers do not come and drag him with a rope bound tight on his legs. The praise names Uma, in whom Brahma, Vishnu and Siva the dancer of the burning ground are one, the trident-bearing virgin, great mother and Gauri, who gave Murugan, and ends at the grove-filled town of Viralimalai where the peacock roams.
583.nuance: காலில் இறுக ... இழாதே: Death's men bind the legs, not the neck, and drag. காவல் என விரைய ஓடி: Murugan is asked to run, the urgency of the plea at the hour of death. ஆதி மறையவனும் மாலும் ... அரனும் இவர் ஒன்றதான ஆயி: the praise makes Uma the one in whom the three gods are united.

source_issues: Chapter 56 is a single song, the remainder of the run under விராலிமலை.
